DOI [10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410) is **“An empirical study on metamorphic testing for recommender systems”**, by Chengying Mao, Jifu Chen, Xiaorong Yi and Linlin Wen (2024). It evaluates six metamorphic relations (MRs) on LibRec, PREA and Surprise, reporting reliability failures and rankings of relations and libraries. Failure detection means observing violations of expected relationships between source and transformed executions. The accessible publisher material does not establish an injected-mutant evaluation or explicit definitions of equivalent mutants, false-alarm rates or testing-cost metrics; those should not be attributed to it without full-text verification.

DOI [10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107807](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107807) is **“Assessing the strength of Metamorphic Testing applied to optimisation software—Experience from industry”**, by Alejandra Duque-Torres, Claus Klammer, Stefan Fischer, Dietmar Pfahl and Rudolf Ramler (2025). It assesses industrial MATLAB optimisation software using MetaTrimmer and mutation testing, rather than recommenders. The [author’s dissertation account](https://dspace.ut.ee/bitstreams/6c3fcccd-43b7-4fe7-9331-3d314e8771d9/download) distinguishes behavioural equivalence from its practical approximation: mutants surviving every sampled input. Assessment compares MR violations against mutants killed by all inputs, then examines partially killed mutants and the test-data volume producing violations. Findings show MR effectiveness depends on the relation, mutant and inputs; surviving sampled tests does not prove equivalence.

Transferable practices, as methodological recommendations: validate MR applicability and constraints first—an inapplicable relation can falsely flag a fault—then report confirmed fault detection, false alarms and execution cost separately. Test-data volume is a sensitivity/workload measure, not GPU time. Neither study establishes that fewer MR violations imply higher HR@10; retain the pinned validation metric for model selection.
